title.en: Describe how a file system stores data

say.en: Imagine your college keeps admissions in one register, fees in another and library records in a third. A student changes her address. How many places must be corrected, and what if one is missed? In this lesson: Describe how a file system stores data.
List the limitations of a file system.

body.en: A file is a container for data stored on a storage device. In a *file system*, each application keeps its own files, often as text or CSV files, and accesses them through programs written for that purpose. This is simple for small amounts of data but creates problems as data grows and is shared.

points.en: Each application has its own files
Access needs a specific program for each file

narration.en: In a file system, each department keeps its own files and needs its own programs to read them. This works for small data but breaks down as data grows.
narration.kn: ಕಡತ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ವಿಭಾಗ ತನ್ನದೇ ಕಡತಗಳನ್ನು ಇಟ್ಟು, ಅವುಗಳನ್ನು ಓದಲು ತನ್ನದೇ ಪ್ರೋಗ್ರಾಂ ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ. ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾದಂತೆ ಇದು ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: Two files, one student: redundancy and inconsistency

say.en: The office keeps a student file. The class teacher keeps a separate attendance file.
Name is stored twice. Storing the same data in many files is data redundancy.
If Asha’s name is corrected in one file but not the other, the copies no longer match: data inconsistency.
Each new question needs a new program, related data sits in separate formats, and anyone with the file can read it.

text.en: Solution: a database with a DBMS

right.en: A new question, like "who has fees due and low attendance?", needs a new program
A student's address is stored in both the fees file and the library file
The address was changed in one file but not the other, so they disagree
Fees are in a CSV file and attendance in a text file of another format
Adding a column to a file forces every program that reads it to change
Teachers should see marks but must not change fees, and the files cannot enforce this

explanation.en: A DBMS removes these problems by keeping related data together once, under one set of rules, with queries instead of special programs and with access control.
explanation.kn: DBMS ಸಂಬಂಧಿತ ದತ್ತಾಂಶವನ್ನು ಒಮ್ಮೆ ಒಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ಇಟ್ಟು, ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರವೇಶ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣದಿಂದ ಈ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗಳನ್ನು ತೆಗೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Difficulty in access: a new kind of question needs a new program. Data redundancy: the same data is stored in many files. Data inconsistency: copies of the same data do not match. Data isolation: related data lies in separate files of different formats. Data dependence: changing a file's structure forces changes in the programs. Controlled data sharing is difficult: it is hard to give different users different access rights.

narration.en: A file system suffers from six problems: difficulty in access, redundancy, inconsistency, isolation, data dependence, and poor control over sharing.
narration.kn: ಕಡತ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಗೆ ಆರು ಮಿತಿಗಳಿವೆ: ಪ್ರವೇಶದ ಕಷ್ಟ, ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ, ಅಸಂಗತತೆ, ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕತೆ, ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ಅವಲಂಬನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯ ಮೇಲೆ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣದ ಕೊರತೆ.

problem.en: A school stores STUDENT.csv (RollNo, Name, Phone) and ATTENDANCE.csv (RollNo, Name, Phone, Date, Status). Identify the file-system limitations.

steps.en: Name and Phone appear in both files → redundancy.
If Phone is updated only in STUDENT.csv, the files disagree → inconsistency.
To list absentees with phone numbers, a new program must be written → difficulty in access.
If a column is added to ATTENDANCE.csv, the programs reading it must change → data dependence.

answer.en: Redundancy, inconsistency, difficulty in access and data dependence.
